sprint1.name: Roster Manifest v2 and Menu Scalability Gate

manifest.generator: tools/expanded_summoning_ideal_roster.py (--check verifies the docs are current)
manifest.isolationProof: expanded-summoning.ideal-roster-isolation asserts no publication, registration, bootstrap, or menu source references the manifest; expanded-summoning.ideal-roster-publishes-nothing asserts every Planned row has no live creature and the visible surface stays at 693.

coverageModel.derivedFrom: ExpandedSummoningCoveragePolicy, over the union of ExpandedSummoningCatalog and SummonNativeExpansionCatalog
coverageModel.whyDerived: An earlier revision stored coverage as literal data filled from the project-owned catalog alone. That marked the eleven retained native-wrapper creatures as though no identity existed, and the tests read the same single catalog so they encoded the omission instead of catching it.
coverageModel.regressionCase: Frost Giant: unit exists as a retained native wrapper and is Published at Summon Monster VIII, while its Nature's Ally VII placement is Planned. Neither half may be collapsed into the other.

menuScalabilityGate.aggregateIsNotOneMenu: 1,232 is spread across eighteen parent spells.
menuScalabilityGate.worstSingleParentNow: Summon Monster VIII and IX: 69 visible choices
menuScalabilityGate.worstSingleParentProjected: Summon Monster IX: 120; Summon Nature's Ally IX: 110
menuScalabilityGate.rubric: R1 stays inside the canvas-safe rect; R2 overflow always offers scrolling; R3 the scroll range spans exactly the overflow with no stranded head or tail; R4 growth costs scroll extent and never viewport height; R5 projected scale behaves in the same shape as baseline scale. Fixed before measuring.
menuScalabilityGate.result: PASS at 1280x720, 1600x900, 1920x1080 and 3440x1440 across the full option-count grid.
menuScalabilityGate.decision: The shipped bounded presentation already clamps to the canvas-safe rectangle and scrolls, and its geometry is option-count agnostic by construction. The existing UI suffices, so no new presentation solution was implemented. The charter permits one bounded solution only when the existing UI is shown to fail; it did not fail.
menuScalabilityGate.liveMeasurementStatus: NOT RUN. The deterministic gate is geometry proof, not a substitute for in-game open/reopen timing, scrolling feel, memory behaviour, or screenshots at projected scale. That evidence requires a guarded runtime scenario with a development-only stress fixture and is disclosed as outstanding.
menuScalabilityGate.deduplicationCorrection: An earlier revision reported 124/112 by adding the tier-9 native wrappers to the 120/110 plan. Those wrapper creatures are roster creatures and were already inside the plan, so the addition double-counted them. One creature is one option whichever catalog supplies its unit.
menuScalabilityGate.gridExecuted: 4 viewports x 200 option counts = 800 evaluations, asserted by count. An earlier revision looped only the first viewport while the evidence claimed the whole grid.
menuScalabilityGate.stressSample: 154 options per parent, labelled a headroom probe rather than a target roster.
menuScalabilityGate.orderingProof: Projected order is run through the shipped SummonDisplayOrderPolicy with synthetic third-party children: singles then 1d3 then 1d4+1, foreign children preserved at the end, and stable across repeated ordering.

sprint2.technicalStatus: AUDIT AND LIVE DONOR OBSERVATION COMPLETE; ASSET IMPLEMENTATION NOT STARTED

findings.viewPolicyLabelIsNotTheDonor: The charter and roster call this a Roc proxy; Roc is the view-policy label, the donor is the giant eagle prefab.
findings.donorIsShared: eagle, dire-bat, pteranodon and roc all use the same donor, so every visual change must be instance-local and reversible. Those three are the sprint's negative controls.
findings.viewSeam: Kingmaker.View.UnitEntityView exposes Animator, nullable CharacterAvatar, AnimationManager, the soft/core colliders, UnitMultiHighlight selection, ParticlesSnapMap, UnitHitFxManager and CameraOrientedBoundsSize.
findings.skeletonTypeIsHumanoidOnly: Kingmaker.Visual.CharacterSystem.Skeleton carries RaceBoneHierarchyObject and CloakScaleFudge, marking it the humanoid Character-doll rig rather than a general creature binding seam. Bone-name matching against it is explicitly not compatibility evidence.
findings.instanceLocalPrecedent: ExpandedSummoningViewScalePatch already does instance-scoped, idempotent, validated view mutation via a Harmony postfix on UnitEntityView.OnDataAttached keyed on blueprint name.
findings.toolchainConfirmed: Unity 2018.4.10f1 (exact game match) plus Blender 4.5.10 LTS, with three shipped deterministic bundles as precedent. All three precedents are static props; a skinned creature mesh bound to an existing skeleton is new ground for this repository.

sprint2.feasibility: FEASIBLE AND NOT BLOCKED. The seam exists, the toolchain is exact and installed, and the instance-local pattern is already shipped and tested.
remainingWork: Live donor inspection through a guarded autonomous observation scenario: confirm CharacterAvatar is null, capture the renderer set, rootBone, bones[] order, bind poses, animator clips, attack/impact events, particle and hit-fx anchors, colliders and camera bounds.
Author an original pterosaur mesh and textures in Blender, rigged to the bone names the live inspection actually reports.
Build a deterministic Unity 2018.4.10f1 AssetBundle with retained editable source and provenance.
Implement safe bundle loading, asset validation, instance-local mesh and bone binding, material compatibility, cleanup and an approved native fallback.
Live acceptance in RTWP and turn-based play across the seven charter scenario groups, with the Roc/Eagle/Dire Bat donor-sharing negative control.
sprint2.blockedOn: Nothing. The remaining work is mesh and texture authoring against the recorded 72-bone rig, a Unity 2018.4.10f1 bundle, the runtime loader with validated fallback, and live acceptance.

liveObservation.characterAvatar: null - plain skinned prefab, not a humanoid Character doll
liveObservation.animatorLocation: child object GiantEagleBoss_Body_RIG_02; UnitEntityView.Animator and m_AnimatorManager are both null until the view attaches to a unit
liveObservation.modellingConstraint: The wing chain is Arm_Upper, Arm_Lower, Palm then six discrete Feather_1..6 bones per side. A Pteranodon carries a membrane on an elongated fourth finger, not six quills, so the mesh must be authored to let those feather bones drive a membrane trailing edge. The four-toed legs need no adaptation.
liveObservation.correctedAssertion: The first run failed an assertion demanding an Animator on the view. That assertion was wrong: animation binds at attach time. It now records the binding instead.

resolvedBlockers.item: Why work when others can do it for you - a guide to Summoning.docx
resolvedBlockers.detail: Supplied by the owner and read. The Pteranodon passage confirms the shipped profile rather than changing it: ten-foot reach valued for attacks of opportunity, and a single main bite on which everything stacks (2d6 plus modifiers). The guide also positions multiple Pteranodons as the best single-target aerial attacker at their tier. This informs Sprint 2's acceptance emphasis on correct bite impact timing and location at Large reach; it changes no accepted statistic.
